title: Tenant burst-state sync gap causing intermittent 429s and cross-environment rate enforcement discrepancies
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments observed sudden 429s and quota rejections during normal traffic patterns between 2025-11-12 and 2025-11-14. Root cause was a synchronization gap between the control-plane policy epoch and the per-node in-memory burst/token-bucket state. In several code paths, a policy update (new burst/quota window) raced with the local token counter migration, leaving nodes with stale negative allowance values that immediately rejected incoming requests until the local state was reconciled. Impact: three paying customers experienced degraded availability (in one case 75% request failure rate for ~45 minutes), causing escalations to Support/CS and at least two pages to SRE. Affected environments: hosted multi-tenant clusters (fast policy rollouts), Dedicated clusters with asynchronous policy propagation, and Private deployments that rely on config pushes (some of which had limited network connectivity to the control plane). Repro steps (internal): 1) Create tenant with burst window = X and steady quota = Y. 2) Generate traffic to consume a portion of the token bucket. 3) Push a policy change that decreases burst allowance and increments policy epoch. 4) On some nodes simulate delayed policy update (network delay / restart) and apply migration logic; observe nodes with allowance < 0 reject requests with immediate 429. Root cause details: The runtime applied policy changes by replacing the rate-limiter parameters and then performing a best-effort migration of counters. A previously overlooked invariant allowed a negative allowance to persist if the local migration path applied arithmetic that subtracted the new max-burst without clamping. Additionally, control-plane to runtime propagation was not guarded by a strict policy epoch handshake: nodes accepted new policies asynchronously and could process requests before migration completed. In Dedicated/Private modes the propagation channel (gRPC push or S3-style config) introduced extra delays, increasing the probability of the race. Short-term mitigation applied: 1) Released a hotfix (runtime v1.21.3) that clamps token counters to [0, max_burst] whenever a policy update is detected. 2) Changed policy application to apply migration before swapping active policy pointer, preventing node from serving requests with inconsistent state. 3) For Hosted tenants, we temporarily slowed policy rollouts to one control-plane region at a time and enabled immediate rollback on error. Permanent fix: 1) Implemented an epoch-based handshake: each policy carries a monotonic epoch id. Nodes will ACK receipt and only transition active enforcement to a new epoch after completing counter migration and writing a durable marker. 2) Added a transactional migration path (write-ahead marker in local metadata store) so restarts will resume migration without producing negative allowances. 3) Introduced server-side enforcement of a minimal grace window where requests are rate-limited conservatively for up to 1s after epoch change to avoid abrupt rejections. Observability & testing improvements: - New metrics: per-tenant policy_epoch, migration_in_progress, counter_clamped_counts. - Console dashboard showing policy rollout progress and per-region migration lag. - E2E chaos tests that inject policy propagation delays and verify no 429s are emitted as a result of migration. - Added unit tests for clamping logic and migration resume. Rollout plan and verification: Hotfix rolled to Hosted within 2 hours of detection (canary -> global) and to Dedicated customers on a stagger (reserved nodes first) with support coordination. Private customers were provided patches and a one-line config change to enable safe migration; two Private customers with air-gapped infra required manual assistance. Verification: dashboards show migration_in_progress -> 0 and clamped_count > 0 for ~30 minutes post-rollout; error rates returned to baseline. Communication & follow-up: - Incident notes published to Confluence and shared with affected customers. - CS held follow-ups and provided credits where SLA thresholds were crossed. - Postmortem meeting scheduled (see attachments). Next steps: 1) Backport epoch-handshake to runtime-1.20 LTS branch. 2) Add a preflight check in control plane to verify propagation paths before large-scale policy changes. 3) Expand observability to alert when migration_in_progress > 30s for any tenant.

2025-11-12 10:05 - hotfix v1.21.3 cut: clamping logic + apply-migration-before-swap. Canary deployed to us-west-2, observed drop in 429 rate on canary tenant within 6 minutes.
2025-11-12 11:20 - deployed hotfix to Hosted global (staggered across regions). Notified Dedicated customers and scheduled reserved-node patching later the same day.

2025-11-12 16:50 - Dedicated rollout: patched control-plane agent and runtime on reserved pools first. One Dedicated customer (AcmeCorp) required rollback for unrelated infra issue; worked with SE to complete patching on second attempt.
2025-11-13 09:00 - Private deployments: shipped patch + migration guidance. Two customers required assisted upgrades due to disconnected artifact mirrors; provided patch tarball and manual runbook.

2025-11-14 14:30 - implemented epoch-handshake design in branch feature/epoch-migration. Integration tests added. Performance microbench shows ~0.6% extra latency during epoch handshake window (acceptable).
2025-11-18 15:45 - merged epoch-handshake into main and started rollout as runtime-1.22-canary. Added console metric 'policy_epoch' to rollout dashboard.
